name: funcoeszz
why: Dozens of obscure shell mini-utilities in Portuguese, a quirky one-of-a-kind toolbox worth an idle browse.

brief.what_it_is: Funções ZZ is a collection of about 190 small command-line utilities for UNIX-like systems (Linux, BSD, Mac OS X, Cygwin), written in shell with bash, sed, awk and grep. Each tool is a short command with a zz prefix, such as zzdolar for the dollar rate, zzcpf to validate or generate a Brazilian CPF number, zzdata for date arithmetic, zzromanos for Roman numerals, or zzrot13 for ROT13. Input comes from arguments or stdin, and output is plain text on stdout. Several tools fetch live data from the web, including exchange rates, lottery results, TV schedules and weather. The homepage says 190 tools, while the README says 'mais de 180' (more than 180).
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no formal problem statement. The homepage describes it as a free, 100% Brazilian, mature project by Aurelio Jargas, built by volunteers 'por prazer' (for pleasure), and its tagline invites visitors to 'Curtiu? Use a versão online ou instale em sua máquina e aproveite!'
brief.how_it_works: The whole collection is shell code using bash, sed, awk, grep and regular expressions. The official release is a single generated file that loads quickly into your shell; the beta keeps each function in its own file under a zz folder, which is slower to load but tracks the newest code. You source the script from your shell profile, and each function then becomes a command you can call directly or pipe into.

commands_seen.context: Validates a CPF number; prints 'CPF válido' or says why it is invalid. With no argument it generates a random CPF.
Date arithmetic: counts the days between today and a given date (example output 13642).
Pipes the numbers 1 to 5 into zztac, which prints them in reverse order.
Looks up the tracking history of a postal parcel by its tracking code.
Given an IP address and prefix length, prints the mask, network, and broadcast address.
Solves a second-degree equation from its three coefficients and prints the roots and vertex.
Converts text to uppercase; README example output is TÁ FUNCIONANDO.
Beta install step: downloads the repository into your home folder.
Beta install step: appends the loader lines to your ~/.bashrc file.
Runs a single function from the official Docker image without installing anything locally (example output shows two DST dates).

brief.install_notes: Via Homebrew, the caveats tell you to add two lines to your shell profile: an export of ZZPATH pointing into the Homebrew opt folder, and a source of that same file. They also say a newer Bash than the macOS default is required. The README's official route is to download the single release file from funcoeszz.net/download and follow the instructions there. The beta route is git clone, then ./funcoeszz zzzz --bashrc, which writes ZZOFF, ZZPATH and ZZDIR settings into ~/.bashrc; ZZOFF lets you turn off unwanted functions. Docker is an option: docker pull funcoeszz/zz. No accounts or API keys appear in the README.
brief.standout: Brazil-specific tools sit alongside general ones: CPF and CNPJ validators, lottery results and random bets, a bicho (jogo do bicho) number lookup, Brazilian city and state lookups, and a parcel tracker. It is all plain shell with no runtime beyond bash, and there is a self-installing zzzz --bashrc command, which is an unusual touch.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as I can tell. The homepage carries a release banner announcing version 21.1 with an announcement and download link, and says the project is 21 years old. I did not see a release date or last commit date, so the exact recency is unknown. Some sample outputs on the homepage are dated 2013 to 2021, so those examples are old.
brief.caveats: Needs a newer Bash than the macOS default, per the Homebrew caveats. Documentation and most examples are in Portuguese, and many tools are Brazil-specific (lottery, CPF/CNPJ, bicho, Brazilian cities and TV), so they are of limited use elsewhere. Several tools depend on live web pages, so they will break when those sites change; I inferred this from the tool names and outputs, not from a README warning. The beta install is slower to load and more manual. The homepage and README disagree on the count (190 versus more than 180). Licensed GPL-2.0-only. Sample outputs on the homepage are dated, so do not treat them as current results.
quotes: Funções ZZ é uma coletânea com mais de 180 miniaplicativos de utilidades diversas, prontos para serem usados na linha de comando de sistemas tipo UNIX
Feito com muito carinho, bash, sed, awk, dedicação, expressões regulares, grep e ♥.
